commits_data.title: dot11decrypt: Use PBKDF2 from libgcrypt
commits_data.message:
dot11decrypt: Use PBKDF2 from libgcrypt

libgcrypt has PBKDF2 support since version 1.5.0 and we are requiring
1.8.0. Also libgcrypt implementation is a lot faster: calculating PSK
5000 times costs 13s with Wireshark internal implementation while costs
5s with libgcrypt version on my workstation.

The only thing should be noted so far is that libgcrypt PBKDF2 does not
allow empty salt(SSID for PSK case) compared to current internal version
and this is not a problem.

Signed-off-by: Chien Wong <m@xv97.com>

commits_data.title: dot11decrypt: Remove a duplicate check againt key type
commits_data.message:
dot11decrypt: Remove a duplicate check againt key type

Dot11DecryptIsPwdWildcardSsid() already checks if the key is of type
DOT11DECRYPT_KEY_TYPE_WPA_PWD. Do not do it twice.

Signed-off-by: Chien Wong <m@xv97.com>

commits_data.title: dot11decrypt: Only derive PSK if SSID is specified when loading keys
commits_data.message:
dot11decrypt: Only derive PSK if SSID is specified when loading keys

Currently we are deriving PSK from WPA passphrases with wildcard SSID
when loading keys. This is useless and wastes significant CPU cycles
since PSK derivation is computationally expensive.

Fix this.

Since this change, we eliminate all PSK derivation with wildcard SSID,
which makes ready for migrating to libgcrypt PBKDF2 since libgcrypt
does not allow empty salt(SSID for PSK case).

Signed-off-by: Chien Wong <m@xv97.com>
